tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit (e.g. an unexplained Evil read, a broken visit claim, or a group result).
tips_feedback.why: I held Erin's Dave nomination and Guilty vote to a concrete census and Chronicler mark, and the Clerk reveal on Dave's death confirmed the choice.

tips_feedback.tip: Yes/No nomination counts are the cleanest liar check, since they cannot be altered.
tips_feedback.why: Carol and I used the 4 Yes total on Dave's nomination to show that Grace's first account of her Day 3 votes was wrong, which forced the correction and shaped the Day 4 hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Vote as you said you would, and explain any switch first.
tips_feedback.why: Grace's early misstatement of her Day 3 votes (No and Innocent, when the totals showed Yes and Guilty) cost her credibility and made her the Day 4 target.

lessons.applies_to: Village roles that might die early (e.g. Archivist, any power role with no result yet)
lessons.tip: Your will is the only channel that survives your death, so write your role claim, any Night 1 info, and your suspicion of who attacked you into it before Night 1. A generic will like 'weigh every claim' gives the town nothing. Frank died on Night 1 with no role information reaching anyone.

Check each player's stated vote against the announced totals before trusting any vote-record argument. The Day 4 Grace dispute was resolved only because the Yes and Guilty counts fit one version of her votes. Do this arithmetic every trial, and treat a mismatch as a lead to question, not as proof.

A single unverifiable claim (a Coroner read, a Chronicler mark, or a census result) should not drive a hang alone. Look for a second source or a death-reveal that tests it. Carol's Chronicler mark on Dave was confirmed only when Dave died and his Clerk role was revealed, which is the kind of independent check the town needed before voting.

With 6 other living players, the Archivist sees 3 roles of which only 3 are real and 3 are fake, so one read is weak. Use it to corroborate a claim you already have, not as a standalone check. Spend the token when it can confirm or refute a specific claim, not on a whim.

When a claim is made on Day 2 and the town is told to wait for a result, make sure the claimant has a way to be checked against a second source. Here, the Day 3 nomination rested on Bob's Coroner read and Carol's mark, and only the Clerk reveal on Dave's death tested either of them.

tips_feedback.tip: Yes/No nomination counts and trial totals are the cleanest liar check; a total above the voter count reveals manipulation.
tips_feedback.why: The announced 4 Yes and 4 Guilty totals on Day 4 let Erin and others show that Grace's first vote record (No/Innocent) could not be right, forcing her correction and making her record the basis for the hang.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit (an unexplained Evil read, a broken visit claim, or a group result).
tips_feedback.why: Bob and Erin cited specific results (Frank Archivist, Alice Census Taker, Dave's Clerk reveal from Carol's mark), and the Day 3 hang of Dave turned out to be correct, so the discipline of naming a specific basis was useful.

tips_feedback.tip: Write your planned target in your will each night, and post results publicly by day.
tips_feedback.why: I had no night target to write (I was killed on Night 1 with no action), so this tip didn't apply to me. For a Night 1 death, the tip misses the key point that a will should carry role and suspicion information, not just a target.

lessons.tip: Before posting any vote or correction, write your exact nomination and trial votes in your notepad and check them against the announced totals. I misstated my Day 3 votes (said No/Innocent when I had voted Yes/Guilty), and the correction cost me credibility when the table was already split. A self-inflicted mismatch looks like a lie even when it is an honest error.

Silence is a liability. Being quiet for two Days with no role or result got me nominated 'for silence' on Day 4. Post a short, concrete status each Day (role or no role, what you did, what you're watching) so nobody can build a case from your absence.

Build a Yakuza read from mechanics, not volume. The Day 3 hang was right because Bob's Coroner result on Frank and Alice's census both pointed at Dave, and Carol's Chronicler mark on Dave came back as a Clerk. Checking which claims share a common mechanical source is what separated true from false here.

Douses persist across nights until an ignite, but a doused player who dies no longer counts toward the 3 living doused needed. Count only living doused players, and plan ignite timing around deaths. Dousing Village players who are being watched by Coroner, Chronicler or Census Taker risks drawing attention, so keep the douse pattern quiet and don't announce it.

A Neutral who is only dousing or waiting to ignite should choose one clear public story early (for example Vanilla with no night action), and keep it. My silence plus changing vote records made me the hang target when Yakuza were already losing.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit (an unexplained Evil read, a broken claim, or a group result).
tips_feedback.why: Erin and Bob tied their Guilty votes on Dave to Alice's census and Bob's Frank coroner result, which made the Day 3 hang concrete and correct. It also exposed my own unsupported Day 4 position, so the table held me to it.

tips_feedback.tip: Vote as you said you would and explain any switch first; a mismatch with the totals is a lead.
tips_feedback.why: The 4 Yes and 4 Guilty totals were used to catch my misstated Day 3 votes. Nobody could ignore the mismatch, and I had to correct it publicly.

tips_feedback.tip: Answer a direct question about your night action in one plain sentence the first time it is asked.
tips_feedback.why: I did not state a role or night result until Day 4, after I was already the target of a nomination for silence. Delay read as hiding even though I had no information to share.

summary:
The Village won 5 to 0 against a lone Yakuza (Dave, Clerk, holding the Katana) and a Neutral Arsonist (Grace).

**How Dave was caught.** On Night 1 Alice's census around Bob covered Bob, Dave and Frank and found 2 of 3 Good. Dave then used the Katana on Frank, a member of that same group. That made Frank look Good, so the one non-Good member had to be Bob or Dave. Bob claimed Coroner and announced on Day 2 that he would examine Frank's body. Dave did not use his Clerk rig and never built a cover story; he went from "no claim" to a bare Vanilla claim. On Night 2 he killed Alice instead of Bob. This hid Alice's Night 2 census (Dave, Erin, Grace: 1 of 3 Good), which would have exposed both evil players. But it left Bob alive to post that Frank was an Archivist. Erin nominated Dave on that elimination logic. Carol's Night 2 Chronicler mark revealed Dave as the Clerk when he was hanged, and he died with his Clerk token unused.

**How Grace was caught.** The Arsonist doused Alice, Erin and Bob but never ignited, even on Night 3 when Erin and Bob were both doused and she was the only player without a claim. On Day 4 she was nominated for staying silent. Under pressure she claimed Vanilla and invented a vote record ("No on Dave's nomination"). Carol and Erin showed that the announced 4 Yes of 5 made that impossible. She then changed her story, and was hanged 3 to 1.

**Decisive plays:**
- Alice posted her census early.
- Bob examined the bodies that settled the case (Frank, then Alice).
- Carol's mark confirmed the Clerk.
- The Village checked claims against the vote totals.

**Decisive mistakes:**
- Dave killed a player inside his own census group, never used his rig, and gave a weak claim.
- Grace never ignited, stayed unclaimed for three Days, and made up a vote record she could not defend.

lessons.tip: Don't Katana-kill someone who shares a group result (census, survey, Diviner group) with you. Katana victims are assumed Good, so each one you kill from the group narrows the suspects toward you. Kill outside the group, or kill the investigator who can confirm the remaining names.
lessons.evidence: Alice's Night 1 census put Bob, Dave and Frank at 2 of 3 Good, and Dave had Katana'd Frank that same night. From Day 2 on, everyone reasoned 'Frank was Katana'd, so it's Bob or Dave.' Once Bob claimed to be Good, Dave was the obvious suspect.

lessons.tip: When a player has publicly promised the next night's confirming result, kill that player, not the one whose result is already public. A dead Coroner can't confirm the body that convicts you.
lessons.evidence: On Night 2 Dave killed Alice, whose Night 1 result was already known. Bob, who had announced he would examine Frank, lived and posted 'Frank was an Archivist' on Day 3. That locked the census onto Dave, and Dave was hanged that Day.

lessons.tip: Spend Day-only tokens such as a Clerk rig before you become the nominee. Rig a Day when you can push a nomination onto a Villager, and have a claim ready that explains the group results against you, not a bare 'Vanilla, no action.'
lessons.evidence: Dave held the Clerk token through Day 2, when nobody was nominated and he could have rigged and pushed a nomination of Bob. He died on Day 3 with the token unused. His defence was only 'three unverifiable claims,' and it lost 4 to 1.

lessons.tip: Once you are the only player without a claim, or the Yakuza are gone and you're the obvious last suspect, ignite with whatever living players are doused that night. A late ignite is better than being hanged with your douses unused.
lessons.evidence: On Night 3 Bob and Erin were doused, 4 players were alive, and Grace was the only one who hadn't claimed. She doused again instead of igniting. She was nominated and hanged on Day 4 without killing anyone.

lessons.tip: Claim a plausible role early, and if you state your votes, make them match the announced totals. Nomination totals are public and can't be changed, so a stated vote that contradicts them is an easy catch, and changing your story afterwards confirms the lie.
lessons.evidence: Grace said 'no claim' through Days 2 to 4 and drew a silence nomination. In her defence she claimed No on Dave's nomination, but it passed 4 Yes of 5 with only Dave voting No. Carol and Erin pointed this out, and Grace's correction did not save her.

lessons.tip: Combine group-count results with the assumption that Katana victims were Good, then use a body exam or a reveal to confirm. When elimination leaves one name and a second source agrees, nominate right away, and say what the mechanical fit is.
lessons.evidence: Erin nominated Dave on Day 3 using Alice's census, Frank's Archivist result and the fact that Katana victims are usually Good. The hang revealed a Clerk.

lessons.tip: Mark the most likely next hang or the most suspicious unclaimed player, so the death reveal confirms the Village's read. Don't spend a token on a player who is already well confirmed.
lessons.evidence: Carol's Night 2 mark on Dave revealed the Clerk on his hanging and confirmed both Alice's and Bob's claims. Her last token, on Night 3, went on Bob, who was already consistent. A mark on the unclaimed Grace would have revealed the Arsonist when she was hanged.

lessons.tip: If a public group result plus a Katana kill already narrows things to one unexplained name on Day 2, weigh hanging that night's suspect then. Waiting a night for confirmation usually costs a power role.
lessons.evidence: On Day 2 Bob argued it was Dave once Frank was assumed Good, but the Village spent all 8 rounds repeating 'wait for Day 3.' Dave used that night to kill Alice, and her Night 2 census (which would have exposed Grace too) was lost.

tips_feedback.tip: Ballots are secret, so keep a notepad of every nomination and trial: each player's stated vote, the announced totals and your own...
tips_feedback.why: Carol and Erin checked Grace's claimed 'No on Dave's nomination' against the announced 4 Yes of 5 and caught the lie. That turned the trial and got the Arsonist hanged.

tips_feedback.tip: Totals can be manipulated... Yes/No nomination counts can't be altered, so they are the cleanest liar check.
tips_feedback.why: The case against Grace was built on the nomination count that can't be changed. Her lie fell apart and her switch made it worse.

tips_feedback.tip: Before voting Guilty, name one concrete mechanical fit: ... a group result where elimination leaves one name.
tips_feedback.why: Erin's nomination of Dave rested on census elimination (Bob claimed Good, Frank an Archivist and a Katana victim), and the hang revealed a Clerk.

tips_feedback.tip: Coroner: Examine bodies that settle live questions... Post the night, target and role in one message the next Day.
tips_feedback.why: Bob examined Frank, which settled the census, then Alice, which confirmed her claim. He posted each result plainly at the start of the next Day, and that made him the trusted voice for both hangs.

tips_feedback.tip: Post your role, target and exact result in your first speech after getting it...
tips_feedback.why: Alice posted her Night 1 census on Day 2 before she was killed. That result was the backbone of the Day 3 case against Dave.

issues.description: Frank's post-game debrief failed: the structured output was rejected five times for missing required properties ('missing_information', 'wanted_but_couldnt', 'bugs_or_oddities', ...), so no answer was recorded. The prompt doesn't make the debrief schema clear to the model, or the harness doesn't recover from the error, and Frank's feedback is lost.

On Day 4 Grace's claim and defense said she voted No on Dave's nomination and Innocent in his trial. In fact she voted Yes and Guilty, and she had said publicly on Day 3 that she leaned Guilty. Players are privately reminded of their own votes, but she still misremembered them. Carol and Erin caught the error by checking the vote totals, and Grace corrected herself only after that. Her claim line also contained a confused note ('Innocent on Dave's trial (no, see Day 3 votes)'). This suggests her own vote history wasn't easy for her to see in her context.

On Day 2 Erin asked Carol whether her Chronicler 'place[d] any mark on Night 2', but Night 2 hadn't happened yet. Dave similarly asked which person Alice's Night 2 result 'adds to' before Night 2 had happened. Both show a mix-up about the phase order (no Day 1; Day 2 comes after Night 1).

On Day 2 Grace said Alice's Good-count census meant 'exactly one of Bob, Dave or Frank is Evil'. A Good count of 2 of 3 only shows that one player is not Good (Evil or Neutral, since Neutrals are never counted). Other players correctly said 'non-Good'.
